sourceInformation.genre: Arcade co-op dungeon crawler, top-down hack-and-shoot
sourceInformation.perspective: Three-quarter overhead, with top-down and isometric in Settings
sourceInformation.tech: my-3D2dge v0.85.2 (handoff, engine unmodified), HTML5 Canvas 2D, Web Audio; AI Hub client 1.4.0 unmodified; tests on Node 24, Playwright 1.63.0
sourceInformation.artDirection: The engine's PS1-era 2D look: procedural rigs, textured floors and walls, canvas lighting, pixel sprites for items, generators, traps and the King; three realms and a banquet hall
sourceInformation.animation: Engine rigs and E.MOVES attacks (overhead swing, throw); bobbing ghosts, lobbed crocks, imp fireballs, the King's phases; gear (axe head, shield, bow) drawn on the rigs. No new move sets.
sourceInformation.audio: Six original songs with a drum layer for the King, sound effects, and Babble voices (a syllable synth) for the narrator and the heroes, all written in code. No audio files. The voices were not checked by ear.
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub shared-world sessions, 1 to 4 players: the host copy runs one world, the others send their player's intents and show its snapshots. Passes the hub conformance round (2 and 4 players, latency, loss, host leave, server host).
sourceInformation.testing: 62 headless checks behind one command (floors, front end, play, dev tools, attract, a scripted playthrough of every stage to the ending run twice, the new mechanics, the letter wheel); the hub harness conformance rounds (standard, latency and loss, host leave, server); the engine browser checker; screenshots
sourceInformation.research: Engine docs (API.md, API-INDEX.md, AI_GUIDE.md), engine source, and the AI Hub README and client; no web research
sourceInformation.environment: Claude Code CLI (headless); Linux; Chromium through Playwright for the browser checks

testingFeedback: About 22 issues. Eight were game-breaking: Escape could not open the pause menu, the pause overlay crashed on Resume, the last stairs crashed into a missing floor, a second run would never show its game over, specials, amulets and skip stairs never spawned, a session skipped its own card so nobody could answer Ready, a touch-only device could start a game, and the shared world had no client path until the hub harness exposed it.

The other fourteen were smaller: autopilot stalls on floors after the first and at the King's gauntlet, a controller symbol default not applied at boot, overlapping quips on the class select, an over-long Dev Tools page, characters the pixel font cannot draw, a join hint over the fullscreen button, aim assist and the camera view not applied at start-up, and headless saves that silently did nothing.
Most helpful test: the scripted playthrough from title to ending, through every stage, run twice.
Least helpful test: the screenshot look notes, which flagged the flat colours of a dungeon.
engineFeedback: Liked most: the TileMap, Humanoid rigs, FlowField and Bullets do the hard parts, and headless advance and input make a whole playthrough run in seconds.

Stuck or guessed wrong: yes. Humanoid weapons are sword, gun and staff only, so the axe, bow and shield were drawn as overlays instead. The pixel font has no middle dot. game.go fades, so tests need settle time. Escape is bound to both pause and cancel. A FlowField keeps its old map after a stage change. The engine's store is empty headless, so the tests supply a memory store. The hub's harness needed unbuffered output from the server.
Built myself: the stage generator with its flood-fill check, the monster, hazard and boss rules, the hero rules, the menu widget, the Babble voices, the songs, and the ghost-mode session.
Hardest: finding supported options, such as Humanoid gear and sound preset names, in the API index and the source, and keeping a moving world's state consistent across scenes.
Engine changes: none. The plan's changes E1 to E8 were not made; each was worked around. See ENGINE-CHANGES.md.
Would change: one list of valid options for each constructor, and the list of characters the pixel font draws.
promptFeedback: Liked most: the run-folder rules, the one-command test rule with failures only, and the done checklist.
Confusing: PLAN.md and TASK.md name the title differently (TASK asks for a pick by RNG), and the done condition asks for every feature while the plan is far larger than one session.
Hardest: keeping to what can be finished and tested rather than the full plan: the full move sets, the King's complete choreography, and a voice synth that sounds right by ear.
Would change: name a must-have slice and say which features the done condition needs, so the rest can be cut openly.

aiHub.name: Gauntletdown
aiHub.description: A one-to-four player co-op dungeon crawl inspired by Gauntlet: blast hordes, smash generators and eat before your life force runs out. Play together on one screen, or in one shared AI Hub world.
aiHub.controls: Move WASD or left stick · Aim mouse or right stick · Fire click, Space or R2 · Magic right-click, Q or △ · Pause Esc or Options
